related_questions.question: What is the new requirement for travel to the UK?

text_blocks.snippet: For US citizens traveling to the UK, an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) is now required, effective January 8, 2025. This requirement applies to those traveling for tourism, business, family visits, or short-term study (6 months or less). The ETA is similar to the US ESTA system and is a pre-clearance measure for travel.

list.title: What is it?
list.snippet: The UK ETA is a digital authorization that allows eligible individuals to enter or transit through the UK without a visa.

list.title: Who needs it?
list.snippet: US citizens traveling to the UK for short stays or transit, who do not have a UK visa or legal residency, need an ETA.

list.title: When did it start?
list.snippet: The ETA requirement for US citizens began on January 8, 2025.

list.title: Where does it apply?
list.snippet: The ETA requirement applies to all parts of the UK, including Northern Ireland.

list.title: How to get it?
list.snippet: You can apply for the ETA online through the UK ETA app or website according to GOV.UK.

list.title: Cost:
list.snippet: The ETA fee is £10 (approximately $13) according to GOV.UK.

list.title: Validity:
list.snippet: The ETA is valid for two years or until the holder's passport expires, whichever comes first according to GOV.UK.

list.title: Important Note:
list.snippet: The ETA is not a visa and does not replace the need for a visa for longer stays or specific purposes like work or study.
